chosen.title: No Robo Bosses: Inside the 13-Day Fight to Make It Illegal for an Algorithm to Fire You
chosen.rationale: California's SB 947 ('No Robo Bosses Act') is sitting on Newsom's desk with a September 30 deadline — a revived version of the SB 7 he vetoed in October 2025, and the first-in-nation attempt to force human oversight before an AI can discipline or terminate a worker. The ticking clock, the veto history, the lobbying, and the documented racial gap in who gets monitored (82% of Black workers vs 65% of White) are exactly Dawn's corporate-capture-of-public-institutions terrain — and distinct from AIMA's existing 'Boss Is a Chatbot' phenomenon piece because it's about the law and who is fighting it.

sources.name: Senator Jerry McNerney — Legislature Approves No Robo Bosses Act of 2026
Bloomberg Law — California's Workplace AI Decision-Making Bill Heads to Governor
National Institute for Workers' Rights — AI Is Not the Boss of Me

rejected_candidates.title: Computer Says Fraud: How Welfare Algorithms Turned Being Poor Into a Crime
rejected_candidates.rationale: Amnesty International's 'Coded Injustice' report on Denmark's fraud-scoring system, the Dutch toeslagenaffaire repayments (~$32,000 to each of 20,000 wrongly-accused, largely immigrant families), and an April 2026 arXiv audit ('Holes in the Public Record') showing governments are hiding these welfare systems from their own AI registers make this a live, escalating story. It is the purest Dawn subject on the board — bureaucracy as violence, opaque black boxes punishing the powerless, class and race baked into the code — and it appears nowhere in the covered list.

sources.name: GIJN — Amnesty International's Investigation of Algorithms in Denmark's Welfare System
UBalt Law — Code and Consequences: How Fraud Detection Algorithms Criminalize Welfare
Lighthouse Reports — Inside a Fraud Prediction Algorithm

rejected_candidates.title: The Town That Said No: How AI's Data Center Buildout Ran Into Local Democracy
rejected_candidates.rationale: In Q1 2026 alone, local resistance blocked or delayed ~75 data-center projects worth ~$130B, with 71% of Americans (Gallup) opposing one in their area — a cross-partisan revolt over secret deals, rising water and power bills, and the absence of community consent, now spreading across four continents. Dawn's angle is the democratic-consent and 'who pays' story, not the carbon math already covered in 'Power Hungry' — following the money and naming who was left out of the room.

sources.name: The Fulcrum — Americans Are Revolting Against the Data Centers Powering AI
Dissent Magazine — After the Data Centers
Waging Nonviolence — The Data Center Fight Is Going Global
